name: Amazon
description: Amazon runs the largest online store in the US and a fast-growing set of services around it, and separately owns Amazon Web Services (AWS), the biggest cloud computing provider. The shopping side earns money three ways: it sells goods itself (online and physical stores), it takes fees from third-party sellers who use its marketplace and warehouses, and it sells advertising to brands on its site, plus Prime subscriptions. AWS rents computing, storage and AI capacity to businesses by usage and long contracts, and earns a margin about five times the retail margin. In FY2025 AWS made 57% of Amazon's segment operating profit from 18% of its sales, and capital spending jumped to about $128B, so free cash flow fell 71%.

businessLines.name: North America
businessLines.how: Sells goods directly, earns fees and fulfilment charges from third-party sellers, sells advertising, and collects Prime membership fees; margin is thin because of shipping and logistics costs.
businessLines.description: Amazon retail in the US and Canada: online stores, third-party seller services, advertising, subscriptions, physical stores (Whole Foods, Amazon Fresh).

businessLines.name: International
businessLines.how: Same as North America: direct sales, marketplace fees, ads and subscriptions, at lower scale and margin.
businessLines.description: Same retail model outside North America.

businessLines.name: AWS
businessLines.how: Customers pay for computing capacity used, often under multi-year commitments; very high margin but needs very heavy capital spending on data centers and chips.
businessLines.description: Cloud infrastructure and AI services: compute, storage, databases, machine-learning services.

brands.name: Amazon Prime
brands.note: Subscription services line was $49,900M in FY2025 (7.0% of revenue); member count not sourced

brands.name: Whole Foods Market / Amazon Fresh
brands.note: Physical stores line $22,711M FY2025 (3.2% of revenue); store counts not sourced

brands.name: Amazon Ads
brands.note: $68,735M FY2025 (9.6% of revenue, up from $55,932M, +23%); sold inside the retail segments, profit not disclosed separately
